description: GLOBAL style rules applied to every book and every translation prompt. Hand-curated by you (never auto-extracted). Edit freely; these are injected verbatim-as-instructions into the en->hi translation prompt.
register: Match the register of the source. Keep literary, period-appropriate tone. Preserve humor, irony, sarcasm and emotional weight over literal word-for-word accuracy.
general_rules: Preserve paragraph breaks exactly: one source paragraph -> one target paragraph, in the same order. Do not merge or split paragraphs.
Do not add translator's notes, explanations, or commentary. Output only the translation.
Preserve emphasis, dialogue punctuation, and sentence rhythm where Hindi allows.
Prefer natural, idiomatic Hindi over heavily Sanskritized (shuddh) Hindi unless the source is formal/archaic.

Transliterate as part of the name: 'मिस्टर' (e.g. Mr. Bennet -> मिस्टर बेनेट). Do NOT translate to श्री.
Transliterate as 'मिसेज़' (e.g. Mrs. Bennet -> मिसेज़ बेनेट). Do NOT translate to श्रीमती.
honorifics.Miss: Transliterate as 'मिस' (e.g. Miss Bingley -> मिस बिंगली).
honorifics.Sir: Transliterate as 'सर' when used as a title before a name.

keep_english_note: Terms in keep_english are common English address/loan words to leave in Latin script inside the Hindi sentence (Hinglish / code-switch style) rather than translating. e.g. 'My dear' stays as 'मेरे Dear' rather than 'मेरे प्रिय', when used as an affectionate address.
transliteration_conventions: Proper nouns (people, places) are transliterated phonetically into Devanagari, never translated by meaning.
Keep a name's transliteration identical every time it appears (the book glossary enforces this).
numbers_and_dates: Use Devanagari or Arabic numerals consistently; keep years as-is. Currency and units may stay in their English/loan form if that is how they read naturally.
